title: Paper weights changed the sign of the mean SO2 abundance ratio in 12 papers from 1981-2003, but its interval crossed zero
abstract: We tested whether a common sulfur dioxide abundance response remained after endpoint selection and equal paper weights. A 2024 public invertebrate workbook supplied 53 count or density records from 12 papers published in 1981-2003. Equal record weights gave a mean log elevated/control ratio of -0.0283. Equal paper weights gave +0.0663, with a 95% t interval of -0.3568 to +0.4894. Seven paper means were negative and five were positive. Equal control-cluster weights gave +0.0567. Single-paper deletions permitted both signs. All three regional and both publication-period intervals crossed zero. Three of six crossed region-period cells had only one paper. No selected paper was published after 2003. Thus reporting structure changed the summary sign, while a common direction remained uncertain. The intervals assume independent paper sampling and do not correct publication selection, detection bias or shared research programmes. Field co-pollutants, different taxa and doses, and publication years limit causal and time comparisons. Climate interactions were not tested. The package includes code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure; source data and detailed extracts remain external.
